purpose: Leakage boundary for using BioGRID ORCS human screens as features/neighbours when predicting Genentech AssayBench. Any ORCS screen id in `excluded_orcs_ids` must never be read, in any form, by a model evaluated on AssayBench validation or test.
matching_rule: EXACT IDENTITY, not fuzzy. AssayBench `dataset_name` literally encodes the BioGRID ORCS SCREEN_ID(s). Four shapes, all 1901 records resolved, 0 unresolved: (a) bare integer -> that ORCS SCREEN_ID (1321 records); (b) U_<id>_{dec,inc,merged} -> ORCS SCREEN_ID <id>, one AssayBench record per hit direction (564 records over 209/179/176); (c) TR_<id1>_<id2> -> BOTH ORCS SCREEN_IDs, a paired screen merged by AssayBench (15 records); (d) U_TR_<id1>_<id2>_dec -> both ids, direction-split (1 record). Verified by pulling every embedded integer with re.findall(r'\d+', dataset_name) and checking the ORCS SCREEN_INDEX row: source_id==SOURCE_ID, author==AUTHOR, cell_line==CELL_LINE, cell_type==CELL_TYPE, library_type==LIBRARY_TYPE, library_methodology==LIBRARY_METHODOLOGY, screen_type==SCREEN_TYPE, experimental_setup==EXPERIMENTAL_SETUP, condition_name==CONDITION_NAME -> 1901/1901 exact agreement on all nine fields, zero mismatches (DURATION agrees 1895/1901; the 6 are the 'Not specified' vs '-' null sentinel, not a different value). No fuzzy matching, no Jaccard tiebreak, and no cell-line name normalisation was needed.

exclusion_policy.publication_level: Exclude every ORCS screen whose SOURCE_ID (PubMed id) is the PubMed id of ANY AssayBench validation or test record. Removes the 359 val/test screens themselves plus 19 sibling screens from the same papers that AssayBench dropped. Same-paper siblings are technical replicates of a val/test screen (same lab, library, batch, often same cell line), so their hit sets are near-copies for non-biological reasons.
exclusion_policy.screen_level: Minimum defensible boundary: exclude only the 359 ORCS screens that ARE val/test records. Leaves the 19 same-paper siblings in. Use only if you need the extra data and say so.
exclusion_policy.strict: publication_level, plus the 14 screens whose max hit-set Jaccard against any val/test record exceeds 0.534 (the empirical ceiling among train-only screens). Investigated: all 14 are Feng X (2022) PMID 35559673 genome-wide essentiality screens in HEK293-A, and the overlap is core-essential-gene sharing with other essentiality screens, NOT experiment identity. Not recommended - it deletes the signal, not the leak.

usable_filter: in safe_orcs_ids AND >=5000 genes measured AND SCORES_SIZE > 1.05*NUMBER_OF_HITS (not a hit-list-only deposit)

verification.metadata_field_agreement: 1901/1901 on 9 fields (source_id, author, cell_line, cell_type, library_type, library_methodology, screen_type, experimental_setup, condition_name)
verification.separation_argument: A genuine val/test duplicate is identifiable: those screens self-match at median Jaccard 0.935 and up to 1.000. Every screen outside the exclusion set tops out at 0.575, inside the 0.534 ceiling set by train-only screens that are independent by construction. There is a clean gap between 0.58 and 0.93, so no val/test screen is hiding in the safe list under a different id.

latest_config.note: The AssayBench 'LaTest' config (19 held-out 2025/26 screens: Perturb-seq, VLP myeloid, CAR-T) has non-numeric dataset_names and none map into ORCS 2.0.18. No ORCS exclusion applies to it. If LaTest is ever scored, it needs its own leakage audit.

depmap.verdict: ZERO. All 697 AssayBench records that come from DepMap/Achilles/Sanger-consortium publications are in TRAIN. No validation or test screen is a DepMap screen, so DepMap gene effect is not label leakage for validation or test. (It IS the same experiment for ~52% of train, which matters for how you fit, not for the test claim.)

cell_line_coverage_of_test.method: exact DepMap CellLineName/StrippedCellLineName, then Cellosaurus synonym, then Cellosaurus HI parent chain
cell_line_coverage_of_test.note: The test split is dominated by hTERT-RPE1 (55), Calu-3 (31), HeLa (21) and primary/engineered lines. HeLa, Calu-3 and Caco-2 are DepMap models with NO CRISPR gene effect; RPE1 and HEK293 are not DepMap models at all. DepMap is a weaker lever on this test set than on train.

depmap.temporal_concern: Not a leakage path, but worth a robustness check. DepMap 24Q4 (Nov 2024) and 26Q1 post-date the 2022+ test screens. There is no information channel from the test publications into DepMap: the gene effect matrix is computed in-house at Broad/Sanger from their own Avana/Humagne/KY pooled screens and does not ingest ORCS, AssayBench or the literature. The control gene sets shipped with it are Hart 2014 / Blomen 2015, which predate everything. So a later release adds cell lines, not knowledge of the test papers. A reviewer can still object to using a 2024/2026 resource to predict 2022 papers; the cheap answer is to re-run the final configuration against DepMap 21Q4 (released 2021-11, predates every test screen) and show the score is materially unchanged. 21Q4 is not on disk and would need fetching from Figshare/DepMap downloads. Do NOT switch to 21Q4 as the primary source: it is CERES-era, has ~1050 lines instead of 1178, and would lose test cell lines. Use 24Q4 as primary, 21Q4 as a stated robustness check.
also_clean: CRISPRInferredCommonEssentials.csv and the Achilles control sets are derived from DepMap's own screens, not from ORCS/AssayBench.
CEGv2 (Hart 2017) and NEGv1 predate all splits.
OmicsCNGene / Model.csv are molecular characterisation, no screen labels.

how_to_use.python: import json; D=json.load(open('engine/splicr/_assaybench_safe_orcs.json')); SAFE=set(D['safe_orcs_ids'])  # then: assert screen_id in SAFE before reading it
how_to_use.hard_rule: Assert membership at the point of read, not at the point of aggregation.

leak_magnitude.measured_on: validation (218 records) only - the test split was NOT touched
leak_magnitude.method: rank each screen's own library-restricted genes by its own ORCS HIT flag then |SCORE.1|
leak_magnitude.interpretation: Reading a screen's own ORCS record scores 0.676, which is 2.3x the oracle-kNN upper bound and 4.1x the LLM ensemble. Any ORCS-derived number above ~0.30 on test is leakage, not a result. This is the reason the boundary is enforced in code rather than documented.

files.note: The safe-only cache contains 1574 screens and physically omits the 378 excluded ones, so a bug downstream cannot read a validation/test screen. No full-archive parsed cache is kept in the repo.
